claims.text: The selective oxidation tendency of X governs whether CrFeCoNiX forms a stable, coherent protective oxide above 900 °C.
Al2O3 and SiO2 are low-strain, well lattice-matched oxides on the corresponding CrFeCoNiX substrates.
Mn oxides have greater expansion or lattice mismatch with CrFeCoNiMn than the proposed Al- or Si-rich oxides have with their substrates.
CrFeCoNiAl and CrFeCoNiSi will develop more adherent and persistent oxide scales than CrFeCoNiMn.
CrFeCoNiMn tends to develop unstable oxide scales that crack or spall.
Oxidative exposure preferentially oxidizes the X element in CrFeCoNiX.
Low thermal-expansion mismatch and strong oxide–substrate adhesion permit a coherent protective layer to develop.
A coherent Al- or Si-derived protective layer retards further oxidation.
High volumetric or lattice mismatch of a dominant Mn oxide causes stress to accumulate during thermal cycling.
Mismatch-generated stress causes oxide-scale cracking or spallation.
Oxide–substrate lattice matching and interfacial structure determine interfacial stress and adhesion quality.
At temperatures above 900 °C, Al- and Si-containing variants will retain stable coherent scales, whereas the Mn-containing variant will show cracking or spallation.
Comparable vacuum thermal treatment produces minimal oxidation.
The proposed behavior applies to both single-phase and multiphase CrFeCoNiX solid-solution states made by typical high-entropy-alloy processing.
The prediction is limited to exposure above 900 °C in oxidative or corrosive atmospheres.
Behavior at lower temperatures or after modified processing may differ.
Minor composition and processing variations may affect oxidation kinetics, scale thickness, and spallation thresholds.
